Question B-003-012-007.

Why the correct answer is right: Overmodulation drives the SSB transmitter beyond its linear range, so the voice becomes distorted and unwanted products widen the occupied bandwidth.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It increases the range of your signal": Any apparent loudness comes with distortion and splatter. It is not a clean range improvement.
- sourceIndex 2: "It occupies less bandwidth and has a poor high frequency response": Overdrive makes the signal wider, not narrower.
- sourceIndex 3: "It has higher fidelity and an improved signal-to-noise ratio": Overmodulation reduces fidelity by clipping or distorting peaks and can worsen interference to others.
